claim: In the ERSET multicenter RCT (n=38, mesial TLE within 2 years of failing 2 AEDs; stopped early for slow accrual), 11/15 randomised to anteromesial temporal resection vs 0/23 continuing AEDs were seizure free during year 2 of follow-up.

bibliographic_record.authors: Engel J Jr, McDermott MP, Wiebe S, Langfitt JT, Stern JM, et al.; ERSET Study Group
bibliographic_record.title: Early surgical therapy for drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy: a randomized trial

supporting_passage: Zero of 23 participants in the medical group and 11 of 15 in the surgical group were seizure free during year 2 of follow-up (odds ratio = ∞; 95% CI, 11.8 to ∞; P < .001).
passage_location: Abstract, Results section. Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 22396514; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/22396514; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.design: multicenter randomized controlled parallel-group trial, 16 US centres, NCT00040326; planned 200, halted early for slow accrual
population_and_design.crossover: 7 medical-group participants underwent AMTR before end of follow-up; 1 surgical-group participant never received surgery
population_and_design.population: mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, age >=12 years, disabling seizures for no more than 2 consecutive years after adequate trials of 2 AEDs (includes adolescents)

endpoint.reported_endpoint: freedom from disabling seizures during year 2 of follow-up (primary)
endpoint.protocol_mapping_v1: freedom from disabling seizures ~ Engel I -> favourable (approximation; to_verify against full text)

reported_observation: 11/15 vs 0/23 seizure free in year 2; QOLIE-89 ITT difference not significant (P=.08); memory decline in 4 (36%) after surgery.
author_inference: Resective surgery plus AED lowered probability of seizures in year 2 vs AED alone; results to be interpreted with caution due to premature termination.
